# Temple Scroll Column 57 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 57 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**57:1** And when he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, they shall write for him this Torah upon a scroll, from the one which is before the priests.

**57:2** This is the Torah which they shall write for him: he shall not [...] and he shall not add to what I command him, and he shall not diminish from it.

**57:3** And he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Me and to keep all these words and to do them.

**57:4** And his heart shall not be lifted up above his brothers, and he shall not turn aside from what I command him, to the right or to the left.

**57:5** So that he may lengthen days upon his kingdom, he and his sons after him in the midst of Israel.

**57:6** And he shall select for himself from them, from all his brothers, one thousand per tribe, to be with him — twelve thousand men of war —

**57:7** who shall not leave him alone, lest he be captured in the hand of the nations.

**57:8** And all the selected-ones whom he selects shall be men of truth and fearers of God and haters of unjust-gain and men of valor.

**57:9** And they shall be with him continually, by day and by night, and they shall guard him from every sinful thing.

**57:10** And from every foreign way, so that he does not fall into their hand.

**57:11** And he shall have a council of twelve princes of his people with him, and twelve of the priests, and twelve of the Levites —

**57:12** they shall sit with him for judgment and for Torah.

**57:13** And his heart shall not be lifted up above them, and he shall not do anything apart from their counsel, any matter at all.

**57:14** And he shall not take a wife from all the daughters of the nations, but from the house of his father he shall take for himself a wife, from the family of his father.

**57:15** And he shall not take upon her another wife, for she alone shall be with him all the days of her life.

**57:16** And if she dies, then he shall take for himself another from the house of his father, from his family.

**57:17** And he shall not pervert judgment; and a bribe he shall not take; and he shall not covet a field or a vineyard, or any property or house, or any desirable thing in Israel.

**57:18** And he shall not rob [...] any of the people.

**57:19** And he shall not amass for himself silver and gold beyond what is needed, only what is sufficient.

**57:20** And when the trumpet of alarm sounds for war, he shall go out before them, and when the trumpet of assembly sounds, they shall gather to him.

**57:21** And he shall take counsel with them and not act alone without their counsel in any matter of war.

---

*EMET notes: Column 57 continues the Law of the King unique to the Temple Scroll. The king's guard of 12,000 (1,000 per tribe) has no parallel in Deuteronomy. The council of 36 (12 princes + 12 priests + 12 Levites) is distinctive to 11Q19. The strict monogamy law (57:15-16) is one of the scroll's most notable features — the king may take another wife only if the first dies. This was likely directed against Hasmonean polygamy.*
